note: This file records every change I (the Vibecoder improvement agent) approved automatically during the long autonomous session. No approval was asked from the user because they were asleep; each entry below was self-approved only because it helps improve Vibecoder. Everything is in plain English so anyone can read it.
approvedBy: autonomous agent (user gave blanket permission for beneficial changes)

entries.what: Create this approvals.json file to record every auto-approved change in plain English.
entries.reason: The user asked me to keep a record of everything I approve automatically so they can review it later.
entries.effect: Adds traceability and trust to the whole session.

entries.what: Initialize a git repository for the Vibecoder project and commit the current working state as a baseline.
entries.reason: Vibecoder had no version control, so every future improvement is hard to review or roll back.
entries.effect: Every improvement from now on is a clean, reviewable git change.

entries.what: Fix provider/model selection: switching provider (--provider or /provider) now automatically uses a valid model for that provider instead of always reusing the GROQ default model.
entries.reason: Sending a GROQ model id to OpenAI, Anthropic or Ollama was guaranteed to fail, so provider switching was broken.
entries.effect: `vibecoder --provider ollama` now correctly uses qwen2.5:1.5b, `--provider anthropic` uses claude-sonnet-4-5, etc.

entries.what: Make the write_file tool create missing parent directories automatically.
entries.reason: The tool description promised it creates parent directories but the code crashed when they were missing.
entries.effect: Writing to new nested paths (e.g. src/utils/deep/file.ts) now works.

entries.what: Harden the agent loop against malformed tool calls: a tool call with no function name now gets a helpful error message back to the model instead of being executed as garbage.
entries.reason: A model sometimes streams an empty tool name; the old code would execute an unknown empty-named tool and create noise.
entries.effect: The agent tells the model to reissue a valid call or finish — no more silent confusion.

entries.what: Refresh the Anthropic model list in config.json to current model aliases (claude-sonnet-4-5, claude-3-5-haiku-latest).
entries.reason: The old claude-3-5-sonnet-latest alias is being retired by Anthropic.
entries.effect: Anthropic provider now defaults to a current, available model.

entries.what: Add tests for the new provider/model logic, file tools, and the malformed-tool-call parser (23 new tests).
entries.reason: Every fix needs regression coverage so future changes cannot silently break it.
entries.effect: bun test now runs 57 tests, all passing.

entries.what: Fix streaming provider tool-call parsing: tool call id and name are now set once (idempotent) instead of being re-appended on every chunk, and the last partial SSE line is flushed before the stream ends.
entries.reason: Multi-chunk tool calls could get mangled ids/names like 'call_abcall_ab', and a final partial chunk could be silently dropped, making tool calls fail only sometimes.
entries.effect: Tool calls now parse correctly for any streaming length (verified live on GROQ: grep + read_file both worked).

entries.what: Add an AbortSignal to the tool context and wire it into the bash tool: Ctrl+C / client abort now kills the running shell (process group) instead of leaving it orphaned.
entries.reason: A hanging command previously kept running after the user aborted, wasting resources.
entries.effect: Cancel is clean and immediate.

entries.what: Make the bash tool actually enforce its timeout: a command that runs too long is killed (whole process group, so grandchildren die too) and the result notes 'timed out'.
entries.reason: The timeout parameter was declared but never enforced — a hanging command could block the agent forever.
entries.effect: Hangs are now bounded and reported as timed out.

entries.what: Harden the grep tool against shell injection: it now spawns grep directly (execve style) with '--' so patterns starting with a dash are safe, and patterns containing shell metacharacters can no longer run arbitrary commands.
entries.reason: The model trusts the user's prompt; a malicious pattern could have executed shell commands on the host.
entries.effect: Patterns like 'x$(touch /tmp/pwned)' are inert (covered by a test).

entries.what: Gracefully report grep/glob failures as clear ERROR messages instead of crashing, and validate config/repl path handling.
entries.reason: A missing directory or bad glob used to throw raw errors out of the agent loop.
entries.effect: The agent gets a readable 'ERROR: ...' result to react to.

entries.what: Add tests for the bash and search tools (13 new tests): output capture, stderr + exit codes, timeout kill, workdir, grep include filter, injection safety, dash-prefixed patterns, missing dirs, and glob behaviour.
entries.reason: The new timeout/abort/injection logic needs regression coverage.
entries.effect: bun test now runs 70 tests, all passing (added --timeout=30000 to the test script because every subprocess spawn costs ~5s in this proot environment).

entries.what: Add scrollback to the TUI: PageUp/PageDown scroll through conversation history (also while the agent is busy), with a live indicator in the status bar (e.g. ↑20/62) showing how far up you are.
entries.reason: Long agent output scrolled off screen with no way to re-read it.
entries.effect: Verified in a real PTY: PageUp 2x then PageDown restores earlier content and the ↑20/62 marker updates correctly.

entries.what: Add an animated spinner (⠋⠙⠹…) plus an elapsed-seconds counter to the status bar while the agent is working, alongside the existing ctrl-c hint.
entries.reason: The old status just alternated two words; a real spinner clearly communicates the agent is alive and working.
entries.effect: Verified under a PTY: frames like '⠋ connecting… 0s (ctrl-c to interrupt)' render and advance during a live GROQ call.

entries.what: Add session persistence: /save [name], /resume [name], /list, /delete <name>, /new commands, an automatic same-conversation snapshot (~/.vibecoder/last.json) saved after every turn and on exit, and a --resume CLI flag. Sessions live in ~/.vibecoder/sessions/*.json and are restored with provider, model, cwd, system prompt and full message history.
entries.reason: Vibecoder had zero memory — closing the app lost the whole conversation, which made multi-session coding work impossible.
entries.effect: Verified live: /save sessdemo + /list work; restarting with --resume restored the conversation and the resumed model remembered and continued the earlier task.

entries.what: Add two new tools: list_dir (directory listing with subdirectories first and file sizes, defaults to the working directory) and fetch_url (transfers an HTTP URL's body as text, with HTTP status, content-type, byte count and a maxChars cap).
entries.reason: The agent could grep/glob but could not see a plain directory listing or read web docs — both are core coding-agent capabilities.
entries.effect: Verified live: the agent used list_dir on src/tools and fetch_url on example.com in one session, correctly.

entries.what: Loop polish: --max-steps CLI flag (bounded agent loop), temperature + max_tokens passed from config into every LLM request, a much richer default system prompt (tool roles, safety rules, retry-don't-give-up guidance), and reasoning_content passthrough for providers that stream chain-of-thought (displayed dimly as '[reasoning]').
entries.reason: Let the user tune how far the agent recurses, keep generation settings in one place, give the model better operating instructions, and surface hidden reasoning from supporting models.
entries.effect: All parameterised from config.json/CLI; verified by tests + typecheck (live reasoning display depends on a reasoning-capable provider).

entries.what: Remove the default max_tokens=4096 I briefly added to config.json — GROQ's free tier limits output tokens per minute to 1000, so it immediately 429-rate-limited every request. max_tokens stays optional/plumbed but is NOT sent unless the user sets it.
entries.reason: A global 4096-token generation ceiling broke the only working provider (GROQ) that has an API key in this environment.
entries.effect: GROQ prompts work again immediately (verified live). Temperature stays configurable.

entries.what: Change the ollama provider baseURL from http://localhost:11434/v1 to http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1 (the server binds IPv4 only, so 'localhost' could fail on hosts that resolve it to ::1). Also strengthen the system prompt with an explicit tool-path rule: paths are relative to the project directory, never prefixed with a leading slash.
entries.reason: The localhost → ::1 ambiguity is a classic silent failure; and a small 1.5b local model produced '/src/tools' during e2e, so the prompt now states the relative-path rule explicitly.
entries.effect: Ollama e2e verified: vibecoder --provider ollama ran list_dir('src/tools') and answered with the correct count of 9 .ts files.

entries.what: Update README: document the session commands (/save /resume /list /delete /new), --resume, --max-steps, PageUp/PageDown scrollback, temperature config option, and the new list_dir / fetch_url tools and net.ts / session.ts modules.
entries.reason: The README documented the app before Phases 3-4 added scrollback, sessions and new tools.
entries.effect: Docs now match the implemented behavior.

entries.what: Fix --resume <name>: named session was ignored whenever last.json existed. The named session is now preferred when an arg is given; a following flag (--prompt etc.) is no longer swallowed as a session name. A clear 'no previous conversation found' message is printed when neither exists.
entries.reason: The original code tried loadLast() first unconditionally, so `vibecoder --resume mysession` always restored the last conversation instead of the named one.
entries.effect: README's promised --resume behavior now works correctly.

entries.what: Wrap handleCommand + runPrompt in try/catch in both TUI and readline onSubmit paths so /provider <invalid> prints a red error instead of silently failing.
entries.reason: An unhandled rejection from createProvider inside an async IIFE produced no user-visible feedback.
entries.effect: /provider bogus now prints 'Unknown provider ...' to scrollback/console and returns to a healthy prompt.

entries.what: Anthropic: merge consecutive tool_result blocks into a single user message instead of emitting separate messages. This fixes the 400 error that occurred when the agent executed 2+ tool calls in one step.
entries.reason: Each tool result was mapped to a separate user message; Anthropic requires all tool_result blocks for one assistant turn to share a single user message.
entries.effect: Multi-tool-step Anthropic sessions now produce a valid message sequence.

entries.what: Anthropic: emit a placeholder text block when a persisted assistant message has no content and no tool_calls, preventing an empty content array that the API rejects.
entries.reason: A resumable conversation could contain an assistant message with content:null and no tool_calls; Anthropic API returns 400 for an empty content array.
entries.effect: Old sessions resume cleanly without Anthropic 400 errors.

entries.what: Normalize tool-call ids across the assistant message and its tool results: a stable id is fabricated when the provider omits one, ensuring consistent pairing on the next API request.
entries.reason: Some providers return empty tool-call ids; the assistant message and tool results must use the same id for the API to pair them.
entries.effect: Tool calls work reliably with providers that omit ids (covered by new tests).

entries.what: Add a default 20s timeout to fetch_url and guard against pre-aborted signals in both bash and fetch_url tools.
entries.reason: A hung URL could stall the agent loop forever; and if a signal was already aborted before a tool started, its listener never fired.
entries.effect: fetch_url is now time-bounded; abort-before-listener races are eliminated.

entries.what: getSize() in terminal.ts: prefer process.stdout.columns/rows (no subprocess spawn) over stty size; keep stty as a fallback when the fast path is unavailable.
entries.reason: Each stty spawnSync has a fixed environment cost; the TTY's own columns/rows are available in a real terminal without spawning.
entries.effect: TUI startup is faster in environments where process.stdout.columns is populated; no behaviour change otherwise.

entries.what: Add 14 regression tests across 3 new/updated files: Anthropic mapToAnthropic grouping (7 tests), normalizeToolCalls id fallback (3 tests), and resolveResumeArg name-vs-flag precedence (4 tests).
entries.reason: Each of the bugs fixed in A022-A028 lacked test coverage; regression tests ensure they cannot re-emerge.
entries.effect: bun test now runs 93 tests, all passing.

entries.what: Add an input token budget to the agent loop (new src/llm/tokens.ts): a `maxInputTokens` config option that trims the conversation history to fit before each request. Trimming keeps the first user task message and the most recent turns, truncates oversized tool results, and clones messages so the saved session is never mutated.
entries.reason: GROQ free tier caps input tokens at 7000/min; a growing conversation re-sent on every agent step quickly exceeded it (the user hit 413 'Request too large, requested 7394').
entries.effect: A 19,776-token conversation is trimmed to ~6,000 tokens before being sent — comfortably under the 7000 free-tier cap, so vibecoder stays usable with no paid tier.

entries.what: Handle 'context too large' (HTTP 413 and wording-matched 400) in both provider clients: throw a distinct ContextTooLargeError instead of a generic hard failure, and have the agent loop catch it, trim the history harder, and retry once.
entries.reason: A 413 previously killed the whole run with no recovery; now it self-heals by shrinking context and re-sending.
entries.effect: Context-too-large errors are transient again: the loop trims and retries automatically (verified by 7 new provider tests).

entries.what: Document maxInputTokens in README config section; update config.json with maxInputTokens: 6000.
entries.reason: Users need to know the knob exists and the default that keeps free-tier GROQ within limits.
entries.effect: Config docs match the new token-budget behavior.

entries.what: Add 17 tests: tokens.ts heuristics + trim behavior (8 tests) and 413/ContextTooLargeError mapping across openai-compatible and anthropic providers (7 tests) plus updated totals.
entries.reason: New token budgeting + 413 retry logic must have regression coverage like everything else.
entries.effect: bun test now runs 110 tests, all passing; typecheck clean.

entries.what: Rewrite trimMessages to trim whole atomic tool-exchange blocks (assistant tool_use + its tool results kept/dropped together) and treat orphan tool results as their own block.
entries.reason: Message-granular trimming could drop an assistant tool_use while keeping its orphaned tool result, which GROQ rejected with HTTP 400 tool_use_failed (observed live).
entries.effect: Trimming can no longer break tool_use/tool_result pairing; lower budget handling reduced to 3-msg floor in extreme-cases test.

entries.what: Recalibrate token estimates: per-char-class conservative weights (CJK~1, letters/digits 0.25, whitespace 0.5, punctuation 0.55). Calibrated live against GROQ real prompt_tokens.
entries.reason: The previous over-weighting under-counted code/JSON-heavy traffic by ~1.26x, so 6000-budgeted requests still hit GROQ's 7000 hard cap with a 413.
entries.effect: Real requests now estimate close to actual: a trimmed 3846-budget request measured 4153 real prompt_tokens, with 2847 headroom under the 7000 cap.

entries.what: Add per-minute input-token pacing: new RatePacer (src/llm/pace.ts) sleeps a free abortable delay before each request so the rolling-minute estimate stays under a provider cap; maxInputTokensPerMinute config opt (default 6500 on GROQ). Also trim to maxInputTokens/1.3 safety factor.
entries.reason: GROQ's 7000 ITPM is a rolling-minute budget, not per-request; even a single large request leaves too little for the next step, and multi-step runs burn themselves on 429s (limit error observed live: Used 2898 + Requested 6295 > 7000).
entries.effect: Multi-step runs pace themselves under free-tier limits instead of failing; the existing 429 backoff remains as a safety net.

entries.what: Add 9 tests: complete pairs atomic trimming regression, tiny-budget pair handling, orphan tool results, RatePacer window/delay/expiry, paceWait no-op cases.
entries.reason: Block-based trimming and the new pacer are core free-tier reliability logic and need coverage like everything else.
entries.effect: bun test now runs 119 tests, all passing; typecheck clean.

entries.what: Add self-knowledge: src/llm/model-cards.ts (honest per-model cards), self_about tool + /about command reporting runtime provider/model, model card, config, tools, and boundaries; setRuntimeIdentity synced on provider/model switches.
entries.reason: Let vibecoder answer 'who/what are you' with facts instead of deflecting — feasible-by-design, honest about unknown fields.
entries.effect: Verified live: agent self-identified as NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra (550B) with correct capacity boundaries from the self_about tool.

entries.what: Add self-edit guardrails: src/self-edit.ts with append-only SELF_EDITS.jsonl audit ledger (before/after SHA-256), isSelfFile/isProtectedFile checks, git-backed restoreSelfFiles; write_file/edit_file block ledger edits and audit config.json/.env self-edits.
entries.reason: Self-modification must be logged, auditable, and revertible without allowing the agent to erase the audit trail.
entries.effect: Live-verified in the real repo: config.json edit was sha-logged and staged, ledger write was BLOCKED, git restore returned config.json to the last approved (committed) state.

entries.what: Add /reload-config (human approve-before-live step), /review-self-edits (ledger + pending diff), /undo-self-edits (reset to git HEAD) REPL commands; inject SELF_EDIT_PROTOCOL immutably into the system prompt.
entries.reason: Guardrails require an explicit human approval step before staged self-edits go live and a permanently-available reset command.
entries.effect: Config.change lifecycle is now: agent edits (audited+staged) → human /review-self-edits → /reload-config (live) or /undo-self-edits (revert).

entries.what: Add 13 tests: model card lookups (exact/substring/unknown), self-edit helpers (path classification, ledger round-trip, limit, shaOf, auditSelfEdit note, summary), file-tool self-edit guardrails (audit on config.json write/edit, ledger protection, no audit for normal files).
entries.reason: Self-knowledge and self-modification guardrails are behavior-critical and need regression coverage.
entries.effect: bun test now runs 132 tests, all passing; typecheck clean.
